selection_dimensions: distinct training family for independent review
deployability at the stated hardware tier

local_three_family.reason: Three separately declared model families that are plausible on local or workstation-class deployments. Receiver policy must still require signed reviews and score them on held-out material.

server_three_family.reason: Current high-capability open-weight candidates from distinct organizations. These are datacenter-scale systems, not phone or ordinary laptop models.

candidates.fit_inference: Best first practical open-weight proposer to test because it combines current generation, manageable scale relative to frontier MoE releases, long context, and standard serving support.
Strong local challenger candidate because the card specifically targets autonomous agentic work and failure recovery, while belonging to a different declared family from Qwen.
Useful third-family local reviewer and cost sentinel. It should not be assumed competent until it passes exact-anchor, abstention, and false-positive controls.
Most straightforward server-class alternative where dense-model behavior and structured output are valued more than local cost.
High-capacity cross-family reviewer candidate when very long laws, dockets, or article corpora matter. Infrastructure cost makes it a server lane, not the default local lane.
High-capability open-weight proposer candidate, but deployment requirements make it inappropriate to describe as a local model.
Frontier-scale cross-family reviewer for long or multimodal source packs. It is not a practical local dependency despite being open-weight.

claim_boundary: Model-card capabilities and fit rationales select candidates; they are not evidence that any candidate can perform Frame Ledger extraction or review. Promotion requires held-out exact-anchor, abstention, challenge, and false-positive results produced by the checked-in adapter contract.
